what: Recto: Hebrew communal letter. Verso: Hebrew-letter-numeral magic square (3x3 grid, letters ב ט ד ז etc., amulet for childbirth) plus Judaeo-Arabic charm text and a few charakteres-like signs at the foot; the square is numerical, no text-structured signs.

Recto (reused leaf, verso is an ordinary Hebrew legal record): ~8 rough lines of hooks, loops, dashes and curls in dense word-like clusters, no recognisable Hebrew or Arabic letters; looks like invented signs or very degenerate scribble. Weak candidate: could be pen-trial scribbling. Needs a closer look.
Recto: Judaeo-Arabic begging letter. Verso (k=2) is a mirror-image ink offset of the recto letter; flipped it reads as ordinary Hebrew-script text, so not a separate text.
Leaf with ordinary Hebrew-script lists/accounts on one side and Arabic-script lines on the other; no unusual signs.

Ordinary cursive Hebrew/Judaeo-Arabic jottings and letter openings over piyyut text, with a line drawing (lamp/stand); verso many scribbles in Hebrew cursive. No invented signs or letter-string structure.
Recto: Aramaic/Hebrew liturgical text (seliḥot) in clear hand. Verso: a few large Arabic-script pen-trial flourishes with small marks. Ordinary.
Very faded Hebrew-script fragment with a crude drawing of a four-legged animal on recto; verso faded Hebrew scraps. Doodle, no cipher.
Recto: Arabic-script pen trials and large doodled letters; verso: Arabic-script note with names and sums. Ordinary.
Recto: grids of short dashes in 4-row groups (geomantic figures/tables) with a few Arabic lines; verso: Arabic names and writing practice. Geomancy tables are divination, not cipher text.
Arabic-script pen trials with invocation (ya ...) and a few letters; verso a few Arabic letters and ink blots.
Arabic-script jottings: names, pen trials, numerals and a cross; ordinary scribbling. Only one image exists.
Recto: faint Hebrew-script lines plus large Arabic flourishes in margin; verso: ordinary Arabic-script lines (state-document phrases). No signs.
Arabic pen trials (basmala), a diamond/star doodle on recto; verso a large flourish and ink blots.
Faded Judaeo-Arabic/Hebrew text on recto; verso a faded Arabic-script list. Ordinary.
Judaeo-Arabic note in Hebrew script; verso a few Arabic-script jottings. Ordinary.
Small slip: columns of Hebrew-letter numerals (e.g. רפב, גנח, תשעה, תפד) with some words and offset/mirror ink; looks like a list of numbers, nothing cipher-like seen, purpose not determinable.
Verso (k=1): rows of repeated samekh pairs (ססס...) as a pen exercise, a Hebrew text on counting (עשר) and Arabic jottings; recto: Arabic-script pen trials. Ordinary.

Recto (k=1) and verso: very large Hebrew letters in 3-line repeating cycle of letter strings (e.g. א ת ח ו ח י ע ו ר / מ ב ט כ ל ו ע ס ף / ק ר ש נ פ ץ) amid scribble and Arabic-script jottings; looks like a letter/scribal drill or possibly a letter-pairing (atbash-like) exercise, cannot tell from the image.
Large rough Judaeo-Arabic/Arabic-script cursive lines on both sides (order of payment/names); letters are ordinary, just roughly written.

Recto: geomancy tables (grids of short dashes/strokes in 4-line figures, a few crosses/hooks at top) above a clear Arabic prayer in 7 lines; verso only stains and a few faint strokes. Geomantic figures are divination notation, not a cipher.
Recto: faded Arabic-script list, repeated lines (amounts) with large ink offset blots; verso: Hebrew note, a Hebrew alphabet-start jotting (אבגדהוז) and ink smears. Ordinary.
Arabic-script text with basmala/invocations and pen trials; verso doodles (menorah, ornamental ovals), a few Arabic lines. No sign system.
Recto: Arabic-script document fragment, 5 lines of cursive (fiscal-looking). Verso: a drawn building/gate with panels and dots plus a short run of Hebrew letters (alphabet practice). Not a cipher.
Recto: large Arabic-script pen trials and looped doodles. Verso: ruled grid of 6 boxes holding faint reversed (mirror-imprint) Arabic-script strokes from another fragment, as the catalogue says.
Both sides: dense overwritten Arabic cursive jottings (basmala, names, pen trials), a small triangular doodle. Not signs.

Both sides: dense Judaeo-Arabic/Hebrew cursive in lines (letter drafts or notes), verso with pen trials, flourishes and a few numerals. Looks like ordinary text; too cursive to read here, but no invented signs.

Tiny scrap (~3 cm). Recto: geometric doodle, a rectangle with zigzag/lattice borders and a triangle with a few wavy strokes; verso: a few faint Hebrew-script lines, mostly illegible. Doodle, no sign system (images are small scraps on a large mount, crops checked).

Recto: Hebrew piyyut in clear hand, Arabic jottings at top and foot. Verso: dense Arabic/Hebrew pen trials, repeated word strings (e.g. ولعو repeated), animal-like blots and a few Hebrew word groups. Ordinary pen trials.
